title: You Shouldn't Have Asked: A Pragmatics-Inspired Taxonomy for Evaluating LLM Refusals
abstract: arXiv:2608.30856v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Refusals are often treated as face-threatening acts in pragmatics because they can challenge the requester's socially claimed self-image. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly trained to refuse unsafe and inappropriate requests, and these refusals may harm users when models fail to manage this interactional cost properly. While existing work has mainly approached LLM non-compliance as a safety-alignment outcome, it does not provide a way to evaluate whether LLMs refuse appropriately across different harmful contexts. To study this question, we propose (to our knowledge) the first taxonomy of LLM refusals that is grounded in pragmatic theory. Applying this taxonomy to responses from 16 modern LLMs across 14 harm categories, we find that although models differ in how they refuse, their refusals are overall explicit and strongly morally evaluative, with interactional repair occurring mainly through offering or providing safer altern

translated_title: 你本不该问的：一种受语用学启发的用于评估大语言模型拒绝行为的分类体系
translated_abstract: 在语用学中，拒绝行为常被视为“威胁面子行为”，因为它们可能挑战请求者在社会层面所宣称的自我形象。大语言模型（LLM）正日益被训练去拒绝不安全和不恰当的请求，而当模型未能妥善管理这种交互成本时，这些拒绝行为可能会对用户造成伤害。尽管现有工作主要将LLM的不服从视为安全对齐的结果，但并未提供一种方法来评估LLM在不同有害情境下是否恰当地进行拒绝。为了研究这一问题，我们（据我们所知）首次提出了一个基于语用学理论的LLM拒绝行为分类体系。将该分类体系应用于16个现代LLM在14个有害类别上的回复，我们发现尽管各模型在拒绝方式上存在差异，但它们的拒绝总体上是明确的且带有强烈的道德评价色彩，其交互修复主要通过提供或给出更安全的替代方案来实现。
tldr: 该论文提出了首个基于语用学理论的LLM拒绝行为分类体系，并发现现代大语言模型的拒绝行为总体上明确且带有强烈的道德评价色彩，主要通过提供更安全的替代方案来实现交互修复。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the first pragmatics-grounded taxonomy for evaluating LLM refusals, finding that modern LLM refusals are overall explicit and strongly morally evaluative, with interactional repair mainly achieved by offering safer alternatives.
